packs.title: Gardens, Angles and Atlantic Air
packs.promise: Find Porto beyond the centre in folded forms, western gardens and open coastal frames.

q.s: Turn contrasting surfaces into three marks of your own.
st: From a stopped public-path position or the official photograph, find one broad stone plane, one folded-looking metal surface and one open gap between sculptural forms. A described example is enough; no counting the whole monument.
Invent a simple nonletter mark for each: one for the plane, one for the fold and one for the gap. Name what each mark stands for in your own three-item legend.
Arrange your three marks into an imaginary signal for someone approaching the garden. Save the signal and its legend; it does not claim to decode the real monument.

q.s: Design a narrow bookmark that borrows a garden’s different heights.
st: Use the official garden map and photographs, or a permitted visitor path in the upper formal garden. Choose one tall hedge edge, one low bed outline and a path separating them; flowers and identifying plant species are unnecessary.
On paper or in a private note, design a narrow bookmark with three bands: tall edge, low outline and a clear path between. Give the path one gentle bend of your own rather than copying a map route.
Add a small blank stopping space to your design and save the bookmark or describe its three bands. This is a paper design, not a game played in the garden or a planted-bed visit.

q.s: Borrow a stone corner for a small paper invention.
st: From the official exterior photographs or a suitable dry public path, choose one angled wall corner and one rounded projecting lookout shape. Looking from a distance is enough.

Design a folded paper holder for an imaginary small treasure: the angled wall becomes one fold, and the rounded shape becomes a flap or tab. The treasure and holder are your inventions, not objects to place at the fort.
Save a drawing or written folding plan with those two borrowed forms. If you have your own scrap paper, you can make it later; nothing is collected from or left at the site.

packs.title: Blue Lines, River Rhythms
packs.promise: Follow blue lines, curious silhouettes and river rhythms through Porto.

q.s: Follow the small decisions inside a tiled wall.
st: Stop where you can comfortably see part of the blue-and-white tiled side wall.
Find a curling painted line, a straight tile seam and a small shape that repeats. You only need one example of each.
Follow the curling line with your eyes. Notice where it turns toward, away from or around another shape.
Save the three details and a short description of the turn you followed.

q.s: See how a red frame holds its shapes together.
st: Choose an open exterior view of the red iron building, outside any event queue or terrace.
Find a substantial support, a thinner repeated piece and a framed opening. Use whichever examples are visible from your position.
Imagine keeping only those lines on a sheet of paper. Describe how the three pieces meet or sit beside one another.
Save your three structural details and one sentence about the pattern they make.

q.s: Give a closed doorway an imaginary delivery.
st: Choose a doorway from a clear public stopping place. Notice one detail of its shape or material without looking inside.
Imagine a small parcel arriving here with something impossible inside: a pocket of sunshine, a spare quiet minute or an idea of your own.
Write a three-line parcel tag with an invented recipient, an imaginary destination and the impossible contents. Let the doorway detail influence one line.
Save your fictional tag and the detail that started it.
